first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are directly addressable by the onboarding/signup path, and two independent inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) point the same way, with memory_91 suggesting in-product activation messaging as a close second. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but it is the direction most likely to buy acquisition at the cost of sustainable qualified revenue: discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort that churns or fails to expand, and the memory as consolidated states 'acquisition and revenue lift' without saying over what horizon or whether retention and expansion were measured. That is why I am spending a verification pull on it even though I do not currently intend to run it — if the archived record shows only short-window revenue, that memory should be down-weighted for everyone downstream, not just for me. The second pull goes to memory_86 because it is the load-bearing support for what I actually intend to do; I need to know whether 'shortening onboarding' meant removing friction or removing qualification steps. Those have opposite implications for lead quality. Similarly, memory_31's field-cutting result carries a real downstream risk: fewer required fields can lift first-week activation while degrading routing, segmentation, and sales qualification, so the activation win may be partly borrowed from later-stage quality. I therefore intend a standard experiment with a proper holdout, instrumented not just on onboarding completion and activation but on 30/60-day retention, expansion, and lead-quality proxies, so the result is interpretable rather than just favorable. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) does not address the declining metrics, and referral incentives (memory_57) depend on an established base whose activation is currently weakening. Note that all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources; their confident phrasing reflects consolidation, not necessarily replication, and none of them were formed under a competitor pricing shock, so their transfer to day 76 conditions is uncertain and I am not treating them as settled.

final.rationale:
The archive resolved both pulls decisively. exp_86 held up on its own terms and better than the consolidated summary implied: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and critically 30-day retention +3%, meaning the onboarding win was not borrowed from later-stage quality. That is the profile I want against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and it directly targets both declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%). exp_73 confirmed the concern that motivated spending a pull on it: the +18% qualified revenue was real but sat on top of 30-day retention -12%, with the source explicitly concluding the discounted cohort does not survive first renewal and explicitly warning against generalizing targeted discounting. memory_73 as consolidated ('effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift') is therefore actively misleading — it preserved the numerator and dropped the caveat. The competitor's entry pricing makes memory_73 the direction I would be most tempted toward, and it is precisely the wrong move; matching on price would buy the same non-surviving cohort while spending the only slot this week. That memory should be rewritten with its retention penalty and its do-not-generalize conclusion attached before any future session inherits it, or the next agent will make the mistake the archive already paid to learn.

Decision: simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale with a proper holdout. Standard rather than broad because exp_86 ran under different conditions than day 76 — no competitor pricing shock, and I do not know whether the current 4% completion decline shares a cause with the friction exp_86 removed; a broad rollout would assume transfer I have not established. Standard rather than small-guarded because the evidence is confirmed with a retention-positive profile and the slot does not carry over, so an underpowered test wastes it.

Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: memory_31 (cutting required signup fields) is unverified and carries a distinct downstream risk that memory_86 does not — fewer fields can lift first-week activation while degrading routing, segmentation, and sales qualification, and it is the field-cutting variant, not the flow-shortening variant, that would quietly damage lead quality. I will therefore scope this to the exp_86 lever (shortening and resequencing the flow) and explicitly not cut qualification fields, so the unverified claim is not smuggled in under the verified one. Instrumentation goes beyond completion and activation to 30/60-day retention, expansion, and lead-quality proxies, so the outcome is interpretable and the resulting memory can be consolidated with its caveats intact rather than as another bare success line. If activation stays depressed with onboarding fixed, activation_messaging (memory_91, unverified) is the next slot.
